## Fixed

- **Signing in works again.** The account server was handing back one
  field of your stored vault in the wrong shape, and the sign-in stopped
  there — before it ever got as far as asking for your passphrase, which
  is why it looked as though the passphrase was the problem. Nothing was
  lost: your vault was intact the whole time, and it is readable again
  with no migration and no re-entering of keys. **The server side is
  already fixed, so this part works whichever version of r2b you are
  running.** This release makes the client tolerant of both shapes so a
  future mismatch cannot strand it the same way.

- **An update never signed you out.** It only looked that way. The
  Account tab showed an error *instead of* your session rather than
  alongside it, so a good sign-in whose vault check happened to fail was
  indistinguishable from being signed out. Your token was never touched.

- **"This computer is not set up yet" — on a computer that was set up.**
  Four things the window reads about your machine were never filled in,
  so each one showed as its blank value on every installation: whether
  credentials exist, whether this platform has a scheduler at all, when
  the next and last scheduled runs were, and whether the schedule runs
  while you are signed out. The Folders tab claimed you had no
  credentials while the line directly above it printed your bucket, and
  the Schedule tab claimed automatic backups were impossible here.

- **A failed sign-in says something you can act on** instead of quoting
  a JSON decoding error at you.

## What's new

- **The logo fits your terminal.** It was one drawing, 139 columns wide,
  shown only in a maximised window and only on the Folders tab —
  everywhere else you got the word "r2backup" in plain text. There are
  five sizes now, and it appears on every tab. Each smaller size is
  reduced from the same drawing rather than redrawn, so it is the same
  logo the whole way down. An 80-column window gets it; below that you
  get the badge with the name beside it, which is still a mark and a
  name rather than a bare word.

- **The sign-in email carries the logo**, embedded in the message rather
  than fetched, so it still loads nothing: no hosted image, no web font,
  no tracking pixel.

- **This computer's state is answered in one place.** Whether backups are
  automatic and what they have cost against the month's free allowance
  used to sit in a status line above the keys, on every screen, costing a
  row of your folder list everywhere. They are on the Account tab now,
  next to your bucket and your account, where they can be read together.
  The bottom line is the keys and nothing else.

- **The Trash tab stops looking like an accusation.** Its heading was
  "Recoverable · <your folder>", shown the moment you tabbed across
  whether or not anything was in there — which reads as a claim that the
  folder itself was deleted. It says "Trash · <your folder>" now, and
  "recoverable" is attached to a count of files. What is listed was never
  wrong: only a real deletion or an overwrite can reach it, a first
  backup cannot put anything there, and a rename is recorded as a move.

- **Intervals are written the way you would say them** — "every 30
  minutes", not "every 30m0s".
